Notes

Intimidation swerves into a restaurant order, ritual spectacle and a chant of self-coronation. The voice keeps choosing when to menace, shrug and let others eat first.

步步紧逼

步步 doubles “step” so that each movement adds pressure. Its clipped four-character shape faces the bodily loss of control in the next line. Repeating this pair makes intimidation mechanical: one person controls the pace, the other cannot control even their own body. The later demand to kneel completes that unequal choreography.

  • Lyric transcript
我还没笑呢

还没…呢 emphasizes that an expected action has not even happened yet. The opponent is already crying before the speaker begins to laugh, so the taunt presents fear as premature and excessive. It is a small contest over timing: the threatening figure claims not only greater strength, but the power to decide when the scene has truly started.

  • Lyric transcript
被害妄想症

This psychiatric term is deployed as a taunt immediately after threats and fear. The speaker first creates pressure, then frames the other person’s alarm as something wrong with them. That reversal is the line’s cruelty. It belongs to the voice’s manipulation of the scene, rather than functioning as a diagnosis of anybody in it.

  • Lyric transcript
一个feat要一个比特币

A guest verse becomes a unit of cryptocurrency: one feat, one bitcoin. The English music-industry abbreviation drops straight into the Chinese sentence, treating the international feature economy as ordinary vocabulary. The deliberately enormous-sounding price establishes distance from the person asking. A few lines later, “I still don’t have much money” punctures the fantasy of effortless wealth.

  • Genius community transcript
小弟娃

弟 already places someone below an older brother; 娃 adds the diminutive sense of a child. The regionally flavored address makes the feature-price boast sound like an older figure brushing off an inexperienced youngster. The insult is about rank as much as money: the other person is too small to negotiate on equal terms.

  • Lyric transcript
没有戏

没有戏 literally says there is no play or performance; colloquially it means something has no prospect of working out. Here it dismisses the other person’s chances immediately after pricing a feature. It need not mean that a literal stage role has been refused.

  • Lyric text
山顶洞人

山顶洞人 is the Chinese name for the prehistoric humans associated with the Upper Cave at Zhoukoudian, near Beijing. In this taunt, that recognizable name is compressed into “caveman,” then coupled with ritual dancing. The historical term supplies the image; the verse is not describing an archaeological practice.

  • Chinese Academy of Sciences: Zhoukoudian Upper Cave research
  • Lyric text
套路

套路 can mean an organized set of moves and, colloquially, a predictable maneuver or manipulative ploy. After the wriggling, silk-spitting spectacle fails to affect him, the speaker asks for simpler 套路. The word makes the display sound rehearsed rather than powerful.

  • Lyric text
底线

底线 is a lowest boundary or basic limit. Placed after extravagant threats and the admission of not having much cash, it separates performative excess from the speaker’s claim to personal standards. The nearby 套路, tricks or maneuvers, are what he sees through; the 底线 is what he says he will keep.

  • Lyric transcript
素三鲜还是地三鲜

三鲜 means “three delicacies.” 地三鲜 is the familiar combination of eggplant, potato, and green pepper; 素三鲜 means a vegetarian trio, with the exact ingredients left unspecified here. After intimidation and the bitcoin feature price, the choice is suddenly an ordinary meal, followed by turning the serving tray and letting others eat first.

  • CCTV 天天饮食: 地三鲜 ingredients and preparation
  • Lyric text
筷子你们先动

Chinese table conversation can refer to beginning a meal as “moving the chopsticks.” After commanding somebody to kneel, the same voice now yields the first move to others at a shared table. The rotating serving tray, indecision over vegetables and small courtesy abruptly bring the self-styled god down to an ordinary communal meal.

  • Lyric transcript
正道的光

正道的光 is recognizable from Huang Bo’s song 正义之道, documented in CCTV’s performance archive. Here its vocabulary of righteousness joins the black-and-white taiji image and the repeated “Lord Kai.” A phrase associated with moral uplift becomes part of an exaggerated personal coronation after the verse’s intimidation, bodily comedy and ordinary meal.

  • CCTV: Huang Bo performs 正义之道
  • 正义之道 lyric text
  • Lyric text
一黑一白太极

太极 is not limited to the martial art called tai chi in English. The explicit black and white also evoke the taiji diagram, a circle of interlocking yin and yang halves. That gives the line a compact visual emblem rather than necessarily describing someone doing exercises.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 太極圖
  • Lyric text
凯神

凯 is the Kai in Zhang Zhengkai, Jackzebra’s name; 神 turns it into a godlike title. In colloquial praise, 神 also marks someone as a master or impossibly good performer. Repeating 凯神 after the “righteous path” and black-and-white taiji imagery stages a compact self-coronation, made more comic by how recently the voice was occupied with ordering vegetables.

  • Apple Music: 青楼 songwriting credits

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
